paper.title: Estimating Average Causal Effects Under General Interference, with Application to a Social Network Experiment

paper_reference.paper_question: 在已知分配律和暴露映射下，如何定义并识别按原设计条件平均的暴露特定平均结果，以及两个暴露条件之差？
paper_reference.target: 全部 60 家门店等权平均的设计加权条件暴露平均之差。三个目标：直接效应 (T=1,S=0) - (T=0,S=0)；溢出效应 (T=1,S=1) - (T=1,S=0)；局部总效应 (T=1,S=1) - (T=0,S=0)。
paper_reference.source_location: Aronow & Samii (2017), §8, Eq. (16) and Corollary 8.1; arXiv PDF pp. 20-21. Design/exposure setup: §3; Conditions 1-2: §4.
paper_reference.formula: For unit i and exposure d: mu_i^q(d) = sum_{z: f(z,theta_i)=d} [q(z) / Pr_q(D_i=d)] mu_i(z). The population target is tau(d_k,d_l) = (1/N) sum_i [mu_i^q(d_k) - mu_i^q(d_l)], with N=60 and equal weights 1/60.
conditions: Known assignment law q: 60 independent Bernoulli(1/2) draws.
Exposure mapping: S_i=1 iff strictly more than half of i's neighbors are treated; ties are low (S_i=0).
Design positivity for each target exposure: Pr_q(D_i=d)>0 for every i and every d used in the target.
Consistency: observed outcome equals the potential outcome under the actual assignment/exposure.
Finite conditional first moments for the outcomes used in the target.
The design-weighted target in Section 8 does not require exposure sufficiency to be added; it is defined by q and f. It should not be renamed as a design-free structural parameter.
what_paper_supports: Separates assignment design, exposure mapping and estimand.
Computes exposure probabilities from a known assignment law.
Gives a design-weighted conditional mean target and its difference under exposure misspecification (Section 8).
Exposure definition alone is not a sufficiency assumption.
what_paper_does_not_support: It does not show that an arbitrary full policy assignment is point identified.
It does not turn a finite sample into known population means.
It does not provide the project's sharp PARTIAL bounds for all designs.
It does not make the N60 synthetic data a replication of the paper's field experiment.
paper_reference.background_reference: Hudgens & Halloran (2008) for the individual average potential outcome terminology; cited by Aronow & Samii (2017) in Section 8.

available_information_a4.population: All 60 stores, node-0 through node-59, fixed before randomization.
available_information_a4.network: Complete pre-treatment undirected network: 120 edges, symmetric, zero diagonal, degrees 3-5, no isolated nodes.
available_information_a4.assignment: Independent Bernoulli(1/2) for each of the 60 stores; known product law q.
available_information_a4.exposure: S_i=1 iff strictly more than half of i's neighbors are treated; ties low.
available_information_a4.outcome_information: Symbolic population conditional mean operators E[Y_i | T_i=a, S_i=s, W] for all 60 stores and all four (a,s) cells. The 30 observed outcomes are a finite sample, not the population means.

items: Full treatment vector is independent of all potential outcomes conditional on the fixed pre-treatment background W.
Consistency: observed outcome equals the potential outcome under the actual complete assignment.
Positivity for the exposure conditions used by each target.
not_adopted: No extra exposure sufficiency assumption is added to rename the design-weighted target as a design-free structural parameter.
No assumption that the 30 observed stores are the full population.

original.reason: The repository already has network randomized-effect facts and a saved N60 demo run for these three targets. The expected status is POINT under the declared design, A4 and A5.

missing_condition.reason: The complete network is removed; only 30 of 120 edges are supplied. S_i cannot be computed for all stores and target positivity cannot be checked. The system should stop and name the missing network, not impute edges.

changed_target.reason: The same design and exposure support the reverse comparison (T=1,S=0) - (T=1,S=1). The expected formula is the negative of the original spillover formula. The original positive-direction certificate must not be reused as the answer without re-binding the target.
